review_type: Author mathematical, instructional and numerical review; no independent specialist certification
chapter_scope: v02-c01 through v02-c04 only; the volume is still being written

v02-c01.reasoning: Checked domain and quantifier order, negation, necessity/sufficiency, empty-domain statements, relation properties, injection/surjection, both budget-set directions, irrationality contradiction, recurrence induction and Bernoulli inequality. Induction includes a base case, arbitrary predecessor and separate gross-factor-one case.
v02-c01.arithmetic: Finite sets, relation counterexample, recurring balances, loan balances, failed inequality and parameter solutions independently recomputed using exact arithmetic.
v02-c01.instruction: Set and relation notation is defined before use. Existence and uniqueness are separated; every requested proof method is demonstrated. Economic implications are kept within model hypotheses.
v02-c01.solutions: All eight prompts have corresponding calculations, proofs or explicit counterexamples. Domain restrictions are repeated where they determine uniqueness.

v02-c02.reasoning: Checked sequence and function-limit quantifiers, domain approachability, limit uniqueness proof, boundedness versus convergence, geometric convergence, continuity, removable and jump cases, theorem hypotheses, root existence/uniqueness distinction and bisection error convention.
v02-c02.arithmetic: Tolerance index, both market roots, five retained brackets, required bisection count, discounted partial sums and smallest acceptable truncation independently recomputed.
v02-c02.instruction: Least-upper-bound reasoning is introduced with a proof and marked for later development. Geometric convergence is justified using the preceding chapter's inequality. Differentiability is distinguished through opposing slopes before full differentiation rules.
v02-c02.solutions: All eight solutions match their domains, strict versus weak tolerances and endpoint conditions. Counterexamples violate the conclusion while exposing the omitted theorem hypothesis.

v02-c03.reasoning: Checked first-principles derivatives, local remainder interpretation, product/chain/quotient rules, elementary-function domains, mean value theorem hypotheses and proof outline, implicit branch regularity, signed elasticity and Taylor remainder conditions.
v02-c03.arithmetic: Cost and average-cost changes, elasticity, implicit branch slopes, exponential and bond approximations independently recomputed. Symbolic derivative values cross-checked by finite differences; printed Taylor errors are within the stated bounds.
v02-c03.instruction: Introduces partial-derivative notation before its limited implicit use and states local branch existence conditions rather than treating formal differentiation as an existence proof. Elementary-function derivative identities are identified as standard results. Units and decimal-rate changes are explicit.
v02-c03.solutions: All eight prompts have full numerical or symbolic solutions, domain restrictions and interpretation. Stationarity, nondifferentiable extrema and endpoint extrema are treated separately.

v02-c04.reasoning: Checked Riemann sum definition, boundedness and integrability assumptions, signed versus absolute area, both fundamental-theorem parts including endpoint continuity, constants on interval domains, substitution and integration-by-parts identities, improper endpoint tests and continuous-flow valuation convergence.
v02-c04.arithmetic: Exact rational rectangle sums independently recover the printed bounds. Smooth definite integrals cross-checked by separate Simpson quadrature. Endpoint-limit expressions, horizons, tails, surplus areas and cost jumps recomputed.
v02-c04.instruction: Defines rate-times-input units and initial conditions. Differentiation, chain and product rules precede their integral uses. Discrete versus continuous timing, economic welfare assumptions and participation jumps are visible.
v02-c04.solutions: All eight prompts have corresponding endpoint evaluations, derivations, convergence decisions or interpretations. Strict tail threshold is expressed as a strict horizon inequality.

shared_review.sources: Official MIT lecture collection and relevant method PDFs retrieved. References are method/further-study routes; chapters contain original economic constructions and exercises. Retrieval dates are 7 October 2026 while the library's edition boundary remains 6 October 2026; no new time-varying empirical claims are introduced.
shared_review.structure: Each chapter contains two worked examples, eight exercises, complete matching solutions, scope/assumption discussion, teach-back, delayed check and source routes. Full HTML build checks links, anchors, source IDs and prerequisites.
shared_review.proof_validation_limit: Proofs were checked by the author step by step; finite numerical samples do not establish universal results. The executable checker expressly limits its scope to numerical results and cross-checks.
